title: Biodiversity action plan

definition.text: A national or local program for protecting and restoring threatened species and habitats, prepared under the Biodiversity Convention.

facts.text: The concept emerged from the 1992 Biodiversity Convention, which asked nations to develop strategies for conserving biodiversity.
A typical plan inventories species or habitats, assesses their conservation status, sets targets, and lays out budgets, timelines and partners.
Plans can focus on species, habitats or agricultural production.
As of 2009, 191 countries had ratified the CBD, but only some had produced comprehensive plans.
A country plan may cost up to 100 million pounds sterling, with yearly upkeep about ten percent of that, which strains poorer countries.
Critics note many plans are pro-forma and almost all overlook fungi, invertebrates and micro-organisms.
Some developing countries object that the plans put wildlife protection above food and industrial production.

related: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan

definition.text: A supplement to the Biodiversity Convention that governs the movement of genetically modified organisms between countries to protect biodiversity.

facts.text: Adopted on 29 January 2000, it entered into force on 11 September 2003; by July 2020 it had 173 parties.
It rests on the precautionary principle of the 1992 Rio Declaration: lack of full scientific certainty is no reason to delay cost-effective protection.
Countries may ban imports of GMOs lacking evidence of safety, and exporters must label shipments of altered commodities such as corn or cotton.
Its Advance Informed Agreement procedure lets importing countries assess risks before the first import of an organism meant for release.
Importing countries may also weigh socio-economic considerations when deciding on imports.
